qt: to the Commission Borja Giménez Larraz (PPE), Raúl de la Hoz Quintano (PPE), Dolors Montserrat (PPE), Isabel Benjumea Benjumea (PPE) Subject:

The rail accident in Urda (Toledo) has raised serious questions about risk management and operational safety when train protection systems fail. Directive (EU) 2016/798 and Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/762 require rail risks to be managed, including those arising from human factors and technical failures. Equally, point 4.2.3.6 of the Annex to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/773 sets out procedures for degraded operation. In light of the circumstances surrounding the accident and potential shortcomings in the transition between train protection systems: 1.

Does the Commission consider that Spain’s supervisory mechanisms comply with the obligations laid down in Articles 4, 9, and 17 of Directive (EU) 2016/798, particularly regarding the responsibilities of rail sector actors and the supervision of safety management systems?
Does it consider that the degraded operation procedures applied in Spain meet EU requirements?

The Independent Administrative Authority for the Technical Investigation of Rail, Maritime and Civil Aviation Accidents and Incidents (AITAT) has recommended three interim measures to strengthen rail safety. In a similar vein, could the Commission also issue interim recommendations to the competent Spanish authorities?
